goldens.comment: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage(), the permission fallback checks for both VIEW and MANAGE scopes (hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)), but canManage() should only grant access for MANAGE scope, not VIEW. This means users with only VIEW permission on groups can pass the canManage() check, granting them write access they should not have. The canView() method correctly checks both VIEW and MANAGE, but canManage() should only check MANAGE.

In getGroupIdsWithViewPermission, hasPermission is called with groupResource.getId() and the same groupResource.getId() is added to granted, but hasPermission resolves resources by name (treating the argument as a group id) and the GroupPermissionEvaluator contract says this method returns group IDs that are later used as UserModel.GROUPS and in getUsersCount group filters. This mismatch means per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions may not yield the expected group IDs for filtering and counts, and evaluation may effectively only look at the type-level 'all-groups' resource; consider revisiting whether this should operate on the underlying group ids (resource names) instead so it aligns with the JPA queries and the interface contract.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:70 — Including VIEW here lets a caller with only all-groups view permission create or promote top-level groups through POST /groups.

This means a user with only VIEW permission on all-groups would pass the canManage() check. In GroupsResource, creating a top-level group calls auth.groups().requireManage() which uses canManage(). This is a security issue where VIEW permission incorrectly grants MANAGE capabilities for group creation operations.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/AdminPermissionsSchema.java:79 — Adding Groups and its scopes only to SCHEMA leaves already-initialized admin-permissions clients without the corresponding persisted scopes and resource after upgrade.

adjudication.rationale: The finding raises a valid concern about schema migration. The diff shows GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE being added to AdminPermissionsSchema with new scopes (MANAGE_MEMBERSHIP, MANAGE_MEMBERS, VIEW_MEMBERS). However, looking at the diff, there's no migration code visible that would add these new scopes to existing admin-permissions clients that were created before this change. The getOrCreateResource method in the schema handles creating resources on-demand, but the scopes themselves need to exist on the ResourceServer. This is a legitimate architectural/upgrade concern, though I cannot fully verify from the diff alone whether there's migration handling elsewhere (e.g., in realm upgrade code not shown). The concern is specific and grounded in the actual code changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:122 — The member-permission scan passes and returns authorization-resource IDs instead of group model IDs, so user searches and counts exclude users authorized through group membership.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at GroupPermissionsV2.java lines 118-127, the getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() method iterates over resources of type GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE and adds groupResource.getId() to the granted set. However, groupResource.getId() returns the authorization resource ID, not the group model ID. The resource name (which equals the group ID based on resolveGroup() in AdminPermissionsSchema.java returning group.getId()) should be used instead. This means the returned set contains wrong IDs, causing user searches filtered by group membership to fail.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/AdminPermissionsSchema.java:250 — Existing V2-enabled realms return before the new Groups resource and scopes are initialized, leaving group permissions unusable after upgrade and exposing null-resource evaluation paths.

The diff shows additions of GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE and related scopes being added to the schema initialization in the constructor (lines 80-85), and a new resolveGroup method. There is no evidence in the diff of any 'V2-enabled realms return before initialization' logic or upgrade path issues. The finding appears to reference code or behavior not present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:121 — Group enumeration crosses identifier domains by returning authorization-resource IDs as group IDs while schema-created per-group resources are not typed for this lookup.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at GroupPermissionsV2.java:121, the code iterates over resources of type GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE and adds `groupResource.getId()` to the granted set. However, examining AdminPermissionsSchema.java, when resources are created via getOrCreateResource(), for groups the resource name is set to the group ID (from resolveGroup which returns group.getId()), but the resource's own ID is auto-generated by the authorization system. The code at line 121 adds `groupResource.getId()` (the authorization resource ID) rather than `groupResource.getName()` (which would be the actual group ID). This is a domain mismatch - the method is supposed to return group IDs but returns authorization resource IDs instead.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:37 — Extending the V1 evaluator-management implementation forces V2 to expose nine inherited management methods that only throw UnsupportedOperationException.

adjudication.rationale: The finding is accurate and grounded in the diff. Looking at GroupPermissionsV2.java (lines 155-211), the class extends GroupPermissions and overrides 9 management-related methods (isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, viewMembersPermission, manageMembersPermission, manageMembershipPermission, viewPermission, managePermission, resource, getPermissions) that all throw UnsupportedOperationException. This is a legitimate architectural concern - the V2 implementation inherits from a class that combines both evaluator and management interfaces, forcing it to stub out methods it doesn't support. This could be addressed by separating the interfaces or using composition instead of inheritance. This is a real design issue introduced by this diff, not a bug but a valid architectural concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:121 — Restricted user searches scan every group resource and run a fresh authorization evaluation for each one regardless of the requested user page size.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a performance concern in the new GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() method at line 121. The code iterates through all group resources using resourceStore.findByType() and calls hasPermission() for each one, which triggers a full authorization evaluation per group. This is O(n) authorization evaluations where n is the number of groups, regardless of how many users are being requested. This is a legitimate architectural/performance concern introduced by this diff, though it's not a bug per se - the code is functionally correct but potentially inefficient at scale.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:61 — Group listings invoke uncached resource lookup and authorization evaluation for every returned group even when one global Groups grant could be evaluated once.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at GroupPermissionsV2.java:61 (the canView(GroupModel group) method), it calls hasPermission(group.getId(), ...) which performs resource lookup and authorization evaluation. In the diff, this method is called via filter predicates like `.filter(auth.groups()::canView)` in GroupsResource.java and GroupResource.java. The finding correctly identifies that for each group in a listing, a separate authorization evaluation occurs. However, the code does have optimization - in hasPermission(), if no specific resource exists, it falls back to checking the 'all-groups' resource type permission. The concern about performance is valid but this is an architectural/optimization concern rather than a bug - the code functions correctly. This is a legitimate performance consideration for the new V2 permissions implementation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:70 — The global canManage check accepts the read-only VIEW scope, so a principal granted view-all-groups can create groups or reparent an existing group through addTopLevelGroup.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at GroupPermissionsV2.java lines 66-73, the canManage() method returns true if hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE). This means a user with only VIEW permission on groups would pass the canManage() check, which is incorrect - VIEW should only allow reading, not creating/modifying groups. The canView() method at lines 48-55 correctly uses VIEW and MANAGE scopes, but canManage() should only accept MANAGE scope, not VIEW. This is a security bug where read-only permissions could allow write operations.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest.java:276 — The VIEW-only all-groups case never attempts a manage operation, so the new canManage path accepting VIEW can grant unauthorized group creation without failing this suite.

adjudication.rationale: The finding misreads the code. Looking at GroupPermissionsV2.canManage(), it checks for MANAGE_USERS role first, then checks for VIEW or MANAGE permission. However, the test testViewGroups() only grants VIEW permission via createAllGroupsPermission(policy, Set.of(VIEW)), and the test is specifically testing view functionality (groups().groups()), not group creation. The canManage() method in GroupPermissionsV2 requires either MANAGE_USERS role OR VIEW/MANAGE permission - but group creation in GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() calls auth.groups().requireManage() which would fail with only VIEW permission since canManage() checks for MANAGE scope specifically for group-level operations. The finding incorrectly claims VIEW grants manage access.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/RealmAdminPermissionsConfig.java:36 — Giving every test admin QUERY_GROUPS bypasses the new permission-based canList path, so policy-only group listing is never verified.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that adding QUERY_GROUPS to the test admin in RealmAdminPermissionsConfig.java means the canList() method in GroupPermissions.java will return true via the role check (root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.QUERY_GROUPS)) before ever evaluating the permission-based path (canView()). This is a legitimate test coverage concern - the new GroupPermissionsV2.canList() logic that checks permissions won't be exercised by tests using this config. However, this is a test coverage gap, not a bug in the production code itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest.java:298 — Granting user and group membership permissions together never proves that each is independently required, so dropping either authorization check would still pass.

adjudication.rationale: The finding points to testManageGroupMembership() at line 298 which creates both an all-users permission with MANAGE_GROUP_MEMBERSHIP and a group permission with MANAGE_MEMBERSHIP, then tests that joinGroup works. The concern is valid - the test grants both permissions together and only verifies the combined result passes. It doesn't test that removing either permission would cause failure, so it doesn't prove both are independently required. This is a legitimate test coverage gap for the new permission logic being added, though it's a test quality issue rather than a bug.
